source.title: BarcodeMamba: State Space Models for Biodiversity Analysis

record.tranche_reason: Applies model scaling measurements to DNA barcode models, a biological sequence setting outside text pretraining. It reports perplexity and downstream accuracy across parameter counts.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. as motivation and reports a parameter-count sweep, but does not fit power laws, test prediction from smaller runs, or study compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Rows cover Table 5’s perplexity and probing-accuracy sweeps. Table 5 fine-tuning accuracy and other ablations are not included as rows here.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out DNA prediction perplexity and downstream classification across model sizes in a new biological sequence setting. Its results bear on V5 and V6, but it does not establish a power-law form or quantitative downstream prediction rule.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that BarcodeMamba scales effectively, especially for unseen-species genus-level 1-NN probing, and acknowledge k-mer overfitting. Their broad description of improving metrics is stronger than the irregular full Table 5 sweeps. Figure 1 emphasises configurations chosen for probing accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: DNA barcode SSMs rather than language models; reports parameter sweeps and task metrics without fitting loss scaling laws or optimizing compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Tokenizer changes the perplexity trend and downstream results: character-level perplexity generally decreases across the sweep, while k-mer perplexity rises at larger sizes; the accuracy series also fluctuates by tokenizer and parameter count.
record.peer_reviewed: Foundation Models for Science Workshop, 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
record.problems: The paper does not fit or compare power-law curves, reports no uncertainty estimates, and shows non-monotonic downstream accuracy and k-mer perplexity trends. It reports only one DNA barcode domain and does not test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocations.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 fine-tuning accuracy values for all 16 tokenizer/size settings were left out to prioritize perplexity and the two pretrained-representation probing measures. Table 1 cross-model comparisons and Tables 2–3 ablations were also omitted because they are not the Table 5 parameter-count sweep.

untested.parts: Natural-language pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens or compute under non-bottleneck conditions.
Fitting small runs and predicting loss orders of magnitude beyond them.
Fixed-compute optimisation and power-law parameter/token allocations.
Depth and width comparisons at fixed parameter count over a wide range.
A fitted power-law loss form, its exponent and adequacy; token and compute scaling; data-sufficient scaling; modalities and regimes beyond this DNA barcode experiment.
A quantitative predictive function, held-out extrapolation, and controlled attribution of task improvements to pretraining loss rather than architecture or training choices.
Sensitivity of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations to setup and fitting choices; systematic departures from a fitted single power law.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted Table 5 values and parameter counts match the supplied text. Row states describing local changes use the preceding smaller model within the same tokenizer and measure as baseline; they do not imply statistical significance. No uncertainty is reported. Model size changes also involve depth, width and batch size, with early stopping up to 25 epochs. Perplexity is exponentiated loss, and perplexities across tokenizers are not directly comparable. No V5 verdict is assigned to the character-level trend because lack of a power-law fit is an untested component, not evidence against the form. Fine-tuning results and other tables were explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: The models are DNA barcode models, not language models; the paper does not test power-law loss scaling in language models.
No prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests parameter scaling of DNA barcode model perplexity, but does not fit or verify a power-law form; does not test image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer settings.
Reports downstream probe accuracy across parameter counts, but does not fit a predictive relation to pretraining loss or evaluate prediction from smaller runs.
Does not compare exponents or fitting choices, or assess systematic curve bending against fitted power laws.

relationships.condition: NTP DNA barcode models with k=6 tokenization, above 7.4 M parameters, on the fixed barcode dataset
relationships.reason: PKM2–PKM8 show held-out perplexity rising from 5.07 to 5.55; authors report overfitting, limiting straightforward transfer of decreasing-loss scaling to this data-constrained regime.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out perplexity increased from 5.07 to 5.55 as models grew, which the authors attributed to overfitting.

relationships.condition: Character-level NTP models, seen-species linear probing, full Table 5 sweep
relationships.reason: LCH1–LCH8 improve overall from 98.4% to 99.3% but plateau and decline locally; these results qualify smooth improvement with scale without testing a prediction rule.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rose overall from 98.4% to 99.3%, with intervening plateaus and declines.

relationships.condition: k=6 NTP models, seen-species linear probing, full Table 5 sweep
relationships.reason: LKM1–LKM8 improve overall from 91.9% to 94.7% but include repeated declines, including 95.8% to 94.7% at the largest size.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rose overall from 91.9% to 94.7%, but repeated declines included a final drop from 95.8% to 94.7%.

relationships.condition: Character-level NTP models, unseen-species genus-level 1-NN probing
relationships.reason: NCH1–NCH8 improve overall but fluctuate substantially; NCH7–NCH8 fall from 61.1% to 58.5% while PCH7–PCH8 perplexity improves.
relationships.display_finding: Performance improved overall but fluctuated, ending with a decline from 61.1% to 58.5% despite improving perplexity.

relationships.condition: k=6 NTP models, unseen-species genus-level 1-NN probing
relationships.reason: NKM1–NKM8 show irregular gains and a final fall from 70.2% to 60.5%; NKM2–NKM7 improve overall while PKM2–PKM7 perplexity worsens.
relationships.display_finding: Performance improved irregularly before falling from 70.2% to 60.5%; earlier gains also occurred while perplexity worsened.
